chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: A movie-house contest prize in Rankin
summary: She sang four shows a day for a week, won a prize of under twenty dollars and a taste of show business.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Ah, so you did get to dance.

Yes. But let me tell you what happened. It was a movie house in Ranken and at the end of the movie the lights would go on and I would charleston for twenty minutes and then the movie would go on again and at the end of the movie I would dance

twenty minutes more. I think I was doing four shows a day. Nobody in the building except me. I'd dance twenty minutes and the movie would show all over again. That was in Ranken, and that was in the twenties. And I did that for a whole week. But I didn't like it. First of all I'm the only thing on the bill. I think I danced to a record or something like that, twenty minutes.
And then the movie. That was my little taste of show business.
Well I hope you took home some money.
Are you kidding? I don't think I got twenty dollars for the week. This was my reward for winning the Charleston Contest.

I'm telling you. Boy, what one will do. Yeah, I remember my grandmother made me a special dress in order to do my act in. I wasn't thinking about acting, being on the stage. I really wasn't hammy, you know, like a lot of people. I was shy for the most part, but I did like to sing, you know?
